2610.07389.title: Inference and learning in sparse autoencoders as natural gradient flow
2610.07389.paper_summary: Sparse autoencoders are widely used to uncover interpretable features in neural networks, yet reliable recovery remains difficult when features overlap or activate infrequently. These challenges involve both inferring which features explain an input and learning the dictionary that represents them. Here, we unify inference and dictionary learning as natural-gradient flows on a shared variational free energy. We instantiate this framework as BeFOND, an encoder-free sparse coding model with closed-form inference and learning dynamics. We show how recurrent explaining away reduces interference between overlapping features, while Fisher preconditioning can compensate for the slow learning of rare features. On synthetic data, BeFOND improves dictionary recovery and rare-feature detection, with a growing advantage over amortized baselines as superposition increases. On language-model activations, it improves single-feature concept detection and selective intervention, outperforming pretrained reference SAEs with substantially less training data. Its feature quality continues to improve with dictionary width, whereas the evaluated baselines largely plateau. Together, these results show how improving inference and learning within a unified probabilistic framework can make better use of data and dictionary capacity to interpret and intervene on neural representations.
2610.07389.paper_summary_zh: 稀疏自編碼器被廣泛用於揭示神經網絡中的可解釋特徵，但當特徵重疊或不頻繁激活時，可靠的恢復仍然困難。這些挑戰涉及推斷哪些特徵解釋了一個輸入以及學習表示這些特徵的字典。在這裡，我們將推斷和字典學習統一為共享變分自由能上的自然梯度流。我們將這一框架實例化為 BeFOND，一種無編碼器的稀疏編碼模型，具有封閉形式的推斷和學習動力學。我們展示了如何通過重複解釋來減少重疊特徵之間的干擾，而費舍爾預處理可以補償稀有特徵的緩慢學習。在合成數據上，BeFOND 改善了字典恢復和稀有特徵檢測，隨著疊加的增加，相對於攤銷基線的優勢不斷增長。在語言模型激活上，它改善了單一特徵概念檢測和選擇性干預，超越了預訓練的參考 SAE，且所需的訓練數據顯著較少。其特徵質量隨著字典寬度的增加而持續改善，而評估的基線則大多趨於平穩。總的來說，這些結果顯示，如何在統一的概率框架內改善推斷和學習，可以更好地利用數據和字典容量來解釋和介入神經表示。
